'''''Yuezhuornis''''' ({{lit|Yuezhuo bird}}) is an [[extinct]] genus of [[Basal (phylogenetics)|basal]] [[avialan]] known from the [[Late Jurassic]] ([[Kimmeridgian]]–[[Tithonian]] ages) [[Nanyuan Formation]] of China.The genus contains a [[Monotypic taxon|single species]], '''''Yuezhuornis yangyuanensis''''', known from a partial skeleton and skull. It has significantly shorter arms than its closest relatives—being proportionally more similar to many non-avialan theropods—implying it was incapable of flight. It was a close relative of ''[[Zhengheornis]]'', which is known from the same locality.

== Discovery and naming ==
The ''Yuezhuornis'' fossil material was discovered during fieldwork in the summer of 2024, in outcrops of the [[Nanyuan Formation]] near Yangyuan Village of [[Zhenghe County]], [[Fujian Province]], China. The specimen is housed in the [[Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology]] (IVPP), where it is permanently [[Accession number (cultural property)|accessioned]] as specimen IVPP V34427. It consists of a highly compressed, partially articulated incomplete skeleton preserved on a single [[Compression fossil|slab]]. Known material includes a poorly preserved skull, components of all regions of the vertebral column, and parts of the {{dinogloss|pectoral girdle}}, forelimbs, {{dinogloss|pelvis}}, and hindlimbs.<ref name="Yuezhuornis" />

In 2026, Xu Liming and colleagues [[Species description|described]] ''Yuezhuornis yangyuanensis'' as a new genus and species of early avialan dinosaur based on these fossil remains, establishing IVPP V34427 as the [[holotype]] specimen. The [[Genus|generic name]], ''Yuezhuornis'', combines a reference to the [[:zh:𬸚𬸦|Yuezhuo]], a mythological bird associated with the [[fenghuang]] (Chinese phoenix), with the [[Greek language|Greek]] word {{lang|grc|ornis}}, meaning {{gloss|bird}}. The [[Specific name (zoology)|specific name]], ''yangyuanensis'', refers to the discovery of the only known specimen in Yangyuan Village.<ref name="Yuezhuornis" />

== Description ==
The ''Y. yangyuanensis'' holotype individual has an estimated body weight of around {{convert|821|g|lb}}, derived from a calculation using the width of the femur. [[Histological]] analysis suggests it was close to skeletal maturity when it died, belonging to a subadult or adult individual.<ref name="Yuezhuornis" />

''Yuezhuornis'' exhibits a combination of features seen in both non-avialan [[paravian]] (i.e., [[troodontid]]s and [[dromaeosaurid]]s) and avialan dinosaurs. The teeth in the {{dinogloss|premaxilla}} (upper jaw bone at the front of the snout) are tightly packed, more like troodontids and ''[[Anchiornis]]'' than ''[[Archaeopteryx]]'' and other avialans, which have widely spaced teeth. These teeth are smaller than those at the front of the {{dinogloss|maxilla}}, another feature more like troodontids and dromaeosaurids than early avialans. The teeth in the middle and rear regions of the maxilla are widely spaced, more like ''Archaeopteryx'' and other early avialans than troodontids. The teeth in the maxilla are serrated along part of their length, a condition not seen in any other avialan. The {{dinogloss|lacrimal}} bone has a much shorter [[Anatomical terms of location#Anterior and posterior|anterior]] process than [[Anatomical terms of location#Anterior and posterior|posterior]] process, as in the more derived avialans ''[[Jeholornis]]'' and some [[enantiornitheans]], but unlike ''Archaeopteryx'' and non-avialan dinosaurs, where the opposite is true. The {{dinogloss|quadratojugal}} process of the {{dinogloss|jugal}} bone is reduced, as in some Cretaceous avialans, but unlike ''Archaeopteryx'', [[anchiornithid]]s, and non-avialan dinosaurs. The slender, rather than robust, {{dinogloss|postorbital}} is also more like early avialans. The {{dinogloss|dentary}} (lower tooth-bearing bone) lacks a groove on its [[Anatomical terms of location#Medial and lateral|lateral]] surface, a feature that characterizes troodontids, dromaeosaurids, and anchiornithids when present.<ref name="Yuezhuornis" />

The {{dinogloss|furcula}} has an obtuse angle, as in ''Anchiornis'' and non-avialan paravians. In early avialans, the furcula has an acute angle. Also unlike early avialans, the {{dinogloss|humerus}} is shorter than the {{dinogloss|femur}}. A longer femur is only seen in some anchiornithids and the flightless [[euornithean]] ''[[Patagopteryx]]''. The {{dinogloss|ilium}} (a pelvic bone) is proportionately much smaller than in non-avialan paravians and later-diverging avialans. The preacetabular process of the ilium is notably longer than the postacetabular process, a condition unique to avialans. Unlike dromaeosaurids and troodontids, but more like early avialans, the foot has a non-[[arctometatarsal]] condition. The last non-[[ungual]] {{dinogloss|phalanx}} of the second pedal (foot) digit is similar in morphology to that of troodontids and dromaeosaurids, indicative of a hyperextensible toe.<ref name="Yuezhuornis" />

To test the affinities and relationships of ''Yuezhuornis'', Xu et al. (2026) included it in an updated version of the [[phylogenetic]] matrix of Wang et al. (2026).<ref name="Zhengheornis" /> ''Yuezhuornis'' was recovered as the [[sister taxon]] to the contemporary ''[[Zhengheornis]]'', a clade Xu et al. named Zhengheornithidae. These taxa are placed within the [[Avialae]], diverging after [[Anchiornithidae]] and ''[[Archaeopteryx]]'', but immediately before the coeval ''[[Baminornis]]''. == Paleobiology ==
The forelimb of ''Yuezhuornis'' combines a long humerus with a short {{dinogloss|metacarpus}}. The forelimb overall is proportionally much shorter than the hindlimb. These features are most similar to non-avialan paravians (which are regarded as being incapable of flight) and flightless birds. This suggests that either ''Yuezhuornis'' lost the ability for flight (thus being secondarily flightless) or that flight evolved twice within Avialae (once in ''Archaeopteryx'' and again in taxa more derived than ''Yuezhuornis''). These features, in addition to the wide furcula, short {{dinogloss|coracoid}}, reduced {{dinogloss|deltopectoral crest}} on the humerus, and long tail, support a terrestrial ecology for ''Yuezhuornis''.<ref name="Yuezhuornis" />

== Paleoecology ==
''Yuezhuornis'' is known from the [[Nanyuan Formation]],<ref name="Yuezhuornis" /> which dates to around {{ma|150|148}}, around the border between the [[Kimmeridgian]] and [[Tithonian]] ages of the late [[Jurassic]] period. The outcrops of this formation have been interpreted as representing a primarily [[swamp]]-like [[depositional environment]]. Most of the vertebrate fossils from the formation represent aquatic and semiaquatic animals, including indeterminate unnamed [[teleost]] fish, [[turtles]], and [[choristoderes]]. Some other avialan dinosaur fossils have also been discovered, including the [[anchiornithid]] ''[[Fujianvenator]]'', the closely related ''[[Zhengheornis]]'',<ref name="Zhengheornis" /> the more derived ''[[Baminornis]]'',<ref name="Baminornis"/> and some additional indeterminate birds, including a possible [[ornithuromorph]] known from a [[furcula]]. This [[lagerstätte]] is collectively referred to as the Zhenghe Fauna.<ref name="Fujianvenator" />
